result.scope: apps/web/src/modules/fleet/components/** (189 files: 184 source files and 5 specs). That covers the dashboard tabs, roster boards, custody parts and letters, fuel boards, reconcile and number-repair screens, alarm cards, hover cards, dialogs, the violations panels, charts and the print-sheet builder. To follow each mechanism I also read the fleet/lib helpers these components call (custody-paper-format.ts, custody-paper-letters.ts, licence-months.ts, custody-memo-editor.ts), the shared/ui and shared/lib modules they import, the Arabic half of the catalogue (i18n.ts lines 15837-31284), and the Fleet specs that pin output from these components. Nothing was edited, built or run, apart from one node -e Intl probe (ICU 78.3).

helpers.name: formatNumber (shared, ar-EG)
helpers.behaviour: In Arabic it uses ar-EG: Arabic-Indic digits grouped with U+066C («١٥٠٬٢٥٠», which reads as one long number). In English it uses en-US («150,250»). null gives «—». Every module uses it, so it must NOT change. Each Fleet caller below moves to a Fleet-local Latin helper instead: latinNumber(v) = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US').format(v), with null giving '—'. That is exactly the 'en' output of formatNumber, so English stays byte-identical. Precedent: VehicleDetailPage.tsx:143-145 (latinNumber). Recommended: promote it into one small Fleet module, e.g. a new apps/web/src/modules/fleet/lib/fleet-latin.ts. The existing `latin` (lib/vehicle-contract-words.ts:24) and `LATIN` (roster/roster-parts.tsx:20) are the same formatter, so either could be reused instead.

helpers.name: formatDate (shared, ar-EG dateStyle medium)
helpers.behaviour: In Arabic it gives «٠٧‏/١١‏/٢٠٢٦» (Arabic-Indic, with U+200F after the day and the month). In English it uses en-GB «7 Nov 2026». null gives «—». It is shared by every module and must not change. Fleet callers move to latinDate(v, locale): Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar-EG-u-nu-latn', {dateStyle:'medium'}) in Arabic, giving «07‏/11‏/2026», and en-GB medium in English (byte-identical to formatDate 'en'). Precedent: VehicleDetailPage.tsx:146-160 (LATIN_DATE / latinDate / latinDateTime), the #767 car page. Alternative for screens whose table already writes year-first «2026/11/07» (receipts, dealership, accidents): locale === 'ar' ? ymd(iso) : formatDate(iso, 'en'), so a dialog matches its row.

helpers.name: ZoomableImage zoom readout
helpers.behaviour: Renders t('fleet.licenseImage.zoomLevel', { value: formatNumber(zoomPercent(zoom), locale) }). The Arabic catalogue value is '{{value}}٪' (i18n.ts:24281), so the reader sees «١٠٠٪»; English shows «100%». THIS COMPONENT IS ALSO USED BY OPERATIONS (operations/components/ShipmentReceiptImageCell.tsx:174), and the catalogue key is shared with it. So the change must be opt-in: add a prop such as `latinFigures?: boolean` (default false, today's behaviour). When it is set, render latinNumber(pct) through a new Fleet key with ar '{{value}}%' and en '{{value}}%' (the en text equals today's). Then pass the prop from the 9 Fleet callers. Operations stays byte-identical.

helpers.name: Custody Word letters' digits: ai / aiAmount / tatweelDate (+ reasonOf, chargeLetterSentence, chargeLetter, fundLetter)
helpers.behaviour: ai (:49-50) maps every Latin digit to U+0660+n. aiAmount (:53) is ai(grouped(v)) with «٫» before piastres: «٨١,٩٠٨», «١٢٤,١٣٩٫٤٦». tatweelDate (:66-69) gives «٠١ـ٠٩ـ٢٠٢٦». In custody-paper-letters.ts they are used by: reasonOf :177 (folds the TYPED reason's digits to Arabic-Indic), chargeLetterSentence :183/:185, chargeLetter :195 and :207 (date «التاريخ ٥/١٠/٢٠٢٦»), fundLetter :278-280 (date lines «التاريخ٢٩/ ٠٩ / ٢٠٢٦» and «التاريخ ٥ / ١٠ / ٢٠٢٦»), :288-292 and :309-313 (body amounts and period), :301 and :321 (table «م» serials, settle row label «تجديد ٥ سياره»), :303 (replenish total). The settle table's amounts are already Latin (latin2). These papers never read the locale (custody-papers.ts:12), so the same Arabic paper shows in both UI languages. Smallest change: make ai return its text unchanged, make aiAmount = grouped(v) (ASCII ',' and '.'), and build tatweelDate from Latin parts. Better still: inline grouped/plain strings at the call sites and delete ai. reasonOf should fold typed Arabic-Indic to Latin with asciiDigits instead of ai, so a typed «٢٤ سياره» prints «24 سياره».

Percent glyph: the Arabic zoom key writes U+066A «٪». Latin digits with the same key read «100٪», which mixes systems. The rest of Fleet writes '%' (fleet-dashboard-tabs.ts:167, CustodyFigures.tsx:46). Use a separate Fleet key whose ar value is '{{value}}%'.

Bidi of dates. ar-EG-u-nu-latn medium carries U+200F after the day and the month («07‏/11‏/2026»). It reads day-first in RTL exactly like today's «٠٧‏/١١‏/٢٠٢٦», but specs or tests that search for a date string must include the RLMs, and a copied value carries them (the Excel text cells in VehicleContractsExport already do today). Never switch an Arabic date to '-' separators (ISO «2026-11-07»): after Arabic text, rule W2 makes the digits AN and the '-' (ES) is not joined, so the parts display reversed («07-11-2026»). '/' is safe (CS between AN joins), as Fleet's ymd «2026/11/07» shows.

The custody letters never read the locale (custody-papers.ts:12). They are one Arabic paper shown in both UI languages, so making them Latin also changes what an English-UI user sees on that paper. This is unavoidable and consistent with «اى ارقام بالانجلش» for his papers, but it is the one place where English output changes. It also departs from his own Word originals (Arabic-Indic, «٫»). Owner pictures are needed: on Linux the paper faces are Arabic-range-only aliases (paper-fonts.ts PAPER_UNICODE_RANGE), so Latin digits now draw from Times New Roman / Liberation Serif rather than the FreeSerif alias. Line counting is by character count (custody-paper-letters.ts:125), so pagination does not move.

reasonOf (custody-paper-letters.ts:177) actively converts TYPED reason digits to Arabic-Indic. Making ai an identity would print whatever was typed, Arabic-Indic included. Fold with asciiDigits so every figure on the paper is Latin.

risks: BIDI: 'ar-EG-u-nu-latn' dates carry U+200F after the day and the month («07‏/11‏/2026»). In an RTL line they read day/month/year, as today. In an LTR context (dir="ltr", <bdi dir="ltr">, a print cell with direction:ltr such as license-expense-memo.ts:182 `.num{direction:ltr}`), the leading Latin «07» resolves to L and stays put while the rest reverses, so the line draws as «072026/11/». The Arabic-Indic (AN) version did not do this. None of the shared-helper callers above sits in an LTR wrapper today (I checked AccidentTransferLogDialog:117, DealershipInvoiceDialog Fact, MaintenanceDialogs, vehicle-print.ts and fleet-report-print.ts, all RTL). Any Fleet-local code that moves a date into a dir=ltr span must strip U+200F or use Fleet's year-first ymd («2026/11/07»). Verify in a picture.

Negative numbers: 'ar-EG-u-nu-latn' prefixes U+200E («‎-250»), and percent style gives «85‎%‎». A spec that matches '-250' literally, or code that parses the text back, will miss. None of the formatNumber callers above formats a negative value today.

Years and identifiers: the Latin formatNumber still groups («2,026», code 1500 → «1,500»). Never route a year, car code, invoice or contract number through it. CompanyViolationsPanel already passes year with String(row.year), which is correct.

Specs that compute their expected text with the SHARED helper (formatNumber(n,'ar'), translate('ar', …, {count: formatNumber(…)})) or with literal ٠-٩ fail once Fleet switches. Re-point them to the Fleet helper or to literal Latin, and keep English pins as they are. Source-text specs survive only if the Fleet helper keeps the names formatNumber and formatDate.

A Fleet-local module with a guard spec (no shared formatNumber/formatDate/formatDateTime/formatBusinessDateTime under modules/fleet; no [٠-٩] in ar values of fleet.* keys; no 'ar-EG' without -u-nu-latn under modules/fleet) keeps the change Fleet-only.

Browser ICU: in Node 22 / ICU 78.3 a bare 'ar' already gives Latin digits, but 'ar-EG' gives Arabic-Indic, and other browser ICU versions may differ for bare 'ar'. Always name the numbering system ('ar-EG-u-nu-latn'), never rely on 'ar'.

Native <input type=date|month|time> boxes in Fleet draw their digits from the browser's UI language, not from any formatter. No shared component can fix that, and on an Arabic-UI browser they may still show ٠-٩. Fleet's DateBox captions are Fleet-local, outside this scope.

Excel: the shared-helper dates in Fleet sheets are inline TEXT cells (xlsx-writer cellXml), so the change only swaps their digits («07‏/11‏/2026»). They are not parsed and nothing is coerced to a number. Numeric cells are untouched.

Fonts: Latin digits fall outside paper-fonts' Arabic unicode-range aliases (paper-fonts.ts:21). On papers they are drawn by Calibri/Carlito, Arial/Liberation Sans or Times New Roman/Liberation Serif at 100% rather than at the Arabic size-adjust. On screen they draw in Azeret Mono (font-figures) or the body face. A paper whose layout was measured with Arabic-Indic digits (the custody letters, which are Fleet-local) may re-flow.

Date order stays mixed across Fleet. The re-pointed formatDate is day-first «07‏/11‏/2026», as VehicleDetailPage's LATIN_DATE already is. Fleet's own lists write year-first «2026/11/07» (ymd). This change only swaps digits; unifying the order is a separate decision for the owner.

Parse-back: none found in scope. Fleet's filters are server-side values, not cell text: Fleet uses no columnFilters or column-filter.ts, and useRememberedFilters stores ISO days. fold.ts and input-rules fold both digit sets, and typed Arabic-Indic digits in ruled inputs or MoneyInput still go in as ASCII.
result.notes:
Bottom line for the shared and platform layer: almost everything Fleet renders from it is already Latin. NumberedPager/FleetPager, MultiSelect, DataTable, BulkActionBar, the error, empty and loading states, toasts, the app shell's badges, translate() and MoneyInput all print raw or nu-latn figures.

Three things put Arabic-Indic in front of an Arabic reader on Fleet screens and papers:
1. The shared formatNumber and formatDate (shared/lib/format.ts:105 and :60), called from 19 and 23 Fleet files: about 70 sites, including the owner's Q2 counts on «السيارات», «التراخيص» and «الإخطارات», workshop and odometer readings, the zoom readout, and the Excel and print dates.
2. Arabic-Indic digits typed into fleet.* Arabic catalogue values, at i18n.ts:23726, 24015, 24781, 24804 and 24836 (live), 22661-22662 (dead keys), and the go-live block 24389-24438 (panel not mounted).
3. One money site that uses the count formatter, CompanyViolationsPanel.tsx:698.

Smallest Fleet-only fix: a new modules/fleet/lib/fleet-format.ts that re-implements formatNumber and formatDate under the same names and signatures with 'ar-EG-u-nu-latn' for Arabic. English keeps en-US and en-GB, so it is byte-identical. Re-point only those Fleet import specifiers, edit the Fleet catalogue values to Latin digits (optionally '{{value}}%' for the zoom readout), and add a guard spec. Shared format.ts and every shared component stay untouched, so HR, ATM, operations, gold, IT, organization, system-admin and the platform home do not change.
